title: Daybreak Signal
brief: Original anime-opening-style instrumental in TV size (about 89 s), 176 BPM: one intro-verse-prechorus-chorus rotation, intro previewing the chorus hook, prechorus modulating up a minor third (D -> F). Melody on a sampled lead guitar with bends; no synth lead or synthetic effects.

sections.intent: Chorus hook on lead guitar and bells over the full band in F; kime on A7 (III of F, V of D) pivots down.
Band riff in D: D-Bb-C-D (an Aeolian cadence) in a gallop locked to the kick; the lead guitar plays the riff line.
A-melo in D: low conversational line over a descending bass; piano and clean guitar, the band from bar 9; authentic cadence.
B-melo: rising long notes; the bass climbs E-F#-G-A-Bb-C and bVI-bVII (Bb, C) become IV-V of F; held leading tone over a break.
Sabi in F, a minor third up: royal-road harmony, kime in bar 8, D6 climax in bars 13 and 17, half cadence at 16, four-bar extension to the tonic.
Hook again, kime on C7sus4-C7, a final F with the last note bent up into pitch and left to ring.

tracks.name: Lead guitar (the vocal line), FSBS dist2
Piano sparkle (VCSL Steinway B, high register)
Drum kit (score in GM numbers; Big Rusty Drums)
String section pad (VSCO sustain, CC11 swells)

decisions: TV-size rotation after Li 2026 (MTO 32.1): verse 16 + prechorus 8 + chorus 16 (+4 extension); the prechorus half cadence modulates up a minor third through bVI-bVII, the most common prechorus-to-chorus move in that corpus.
Intro = chorus hook in the chorus key, pivoting to the verse key on A7 (III of F acting as V of D).
Chorus: hook F-E-F-E with a G anticipated across the bar; second phrase a third higher on the maj7 of IV; royal-road third phrase to C6; D6 peaks in bars 13 and 17; half cadence on C7 at bar 16.
Lead guitar bends: D6 peaks and the final note bent up a whole step into pitch, slides into phrase starts, upward vibrato on held notes (performance.bend, range 12).

Two-bar accompaniment units accented with the kick, kime in intro bar 8, chorus bar 8 and outro bar 6, breaks before the chorus and at the half cadence, 16th sparkle and crash quarters in the chorus second half.
No synth lead and no noise risers or impacts; the sub layer under the bass is the only synthesized part.
Fewer stops: after an anticipation the bass and left guitar keep driving in eighths (only held chords tie over), strums last 96% of the note, the riff drives in 3+3+2 eighths.
